spec.name: gbm_all_news
spec.notes: Hypothesis: short-term reversal (the lab's strongest single signal, ret_1w) mixes two kinds of moves. Moves without public news are mostly liquidity-driven and reverse; moves on news days are information and drift (Chan 2003, JFE 70:223-260; Jiang, Li & Wang 2021, JFE 141:573-599). Splitting last week's return into a no-news part (sessions without an SEC 8-K/10-Q/10-K, sign -1) and a one-month news-day drift part (sign +1) should give the model a purer reversal signal. Comparison: identical to the pre-registered gbm_all except for these two features (new 'news' family, so no existing model changes). Expected effect: higher development IC than gbm_all (0.0187) and more of the gross long-short surviving costs, because fewer trades are spent fading news moves that keep going. SEC filings are only firm-issued news, so the split is noisy and the effect may be small.

spec.name: gbm_all_season
spec.notes: Hypothesis: stocks that did well relative to others in a given calendar month tend to do so again in that month, and correspondingly worse in other months (Heston & Sadka 2008, JFE 87:418-445; Keloharju, Linnainmaa & Nyberg 2021, JFE 139:138-161, whose same-month-minus-other-months factor has t = 9.9 over 1963-2016 and was positive in every 10-year window). season_amn uses only completed months 1-10 years back and is unrelated to every existing feature (none uses calendar position). It changes once a month, so it can help the model hold or time names rather than add weekly turnover; KLN note seasonalities are too high-turnover to trade alone but useful for timing trades. Comparison: identical to the pre-registered gbm_all except for this feature (new 'seasonal' family). Expected effect: small IC gain (published monthly spreads imply a 5-day IC well under 0.01) with no increase in turnover. Risk: post-publication decay and survivor-only Yahoo history.

spec.name: gbm_all_season_residrev
spec.notes: Hypothesis: the reversal family is the core of the learned models (dropping it cuts dev IC t from 5.6 to 3.8), but raw reversal is mostly a bet on recent factor and industry moves, and its edge is too small for its trading costs (gbm_all_season: gross hysteresis long-short +8.7%/yr, net +0.2%). Blitz, Huij, Lansdorp & Verbeek (2013, J. Financial Markets 16(3):477-504) show that reversal measured on factor-model residuals and scaled by residual volatility earns about twice the risk-adjusted return of conventional reversal, trades less in small volatile names, and survives costs: in the 500 largest US stocks the break-even round-trip cost is ~48 bp vs ~18 bp for conventional reversal (Keim-Madhavan costs, 1990-2008). Da, Liu & Schaumburg (2014, Management Science 60(3):658-674) find the reversal comes from the non-fundamental part of the move. resid_rev_1m removes market and statistical-industry exposure with betas estimated over the year before the formation month and divides the residual month by residual volatility (new 'residual' family; no existing model changes). Comparison: identical to gbm_all_season (best development model, IC t 5.63) except for this one feature. Success: dev IC t at least equal to gbm_all_season's and a higher net hysteresis long-short (> +2%/yr), with the gates passed. Failure: no IC gain or no net gain (the feature is ~collinear with ind_rel_1m + ivol_3m, which the trees already combine). Risk: survivor-only Yahoo history flatters reversal-type signals.

spec.name: gbm_all_season_stmom
spec.notes: Hypothesis: last month's return means different things for stocks that traded heavily and lightly. Medhat & Schmeling (2022, Review of Financial Studies 35(3):1480-1526): among the highest-turnover stocks (volume / shares outstanding) last month's winners keep winning (short-term momentum, ~1.4%/month, persists ~12 months, survives half-spread costs, strongest in large liquid stocks), while among low-turnover stocks they reverse. Mechanism: heavy trading signals information-driven moves that are underreacted to; light-trading moves are liquidity shocks that revert. The trees cannot form turnover from log_dvol and log_mcap easily (it is their difference), so turnover_1m (average daily dollar volume over market value, needs SEC share counts) and stmom_1m (centred rank of 1-month return times centred rank of turnover) are added explicitly in a new 'turnover' family (no existing model changes). Because the high-turnover winner signal is persistent, it should help the model hold names longer, i.e. lower turnover per unit of IC. Comparison: identical to gbm_all_season except for these two features. Success: dev IC t at least equal to gbm_all_season's with a higher net hysteresis long-short (> +2%/yr) and gates passed. Failure: no IC or net gain. Caveat: the paper's weekly-formation version loses money (price pressure), and its sorts are monthly, so the 5-day effect may be small.

spec.name: rule_exit80
spec.notes: Keep a held name until it falls below rank 80 instead of 40 (wider no-trade band). Novy-Marx & Velikov (2016, RFS) buy/hold spread; DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera, Nogales & Uppal (2020, RFS).

spec.name: rule_hold10
spec.notes: Trade every 10 sessions instead of 5; holdings are left alone at the in-between rebalance. Novy-Marx & Velikov (2016, RFS); Garleanu & Pedersen (2013, JF).

spec.name: rule_hold10_exit80
spec.notes: Rules hold10 and exit80 together: trade less often and less per trade. Garleanu & Pedersen (2013, JF).

spec.name: rule_n20
spec.notes: 20 names, keep until rank 80, at most 6 per statistical sector: the current 10/40/3 scaled to 20 names. DeMiguel et al. (2020, RFS).
